name: q31-earliest-store-is-working
source:
let x = "s"
x = 1
exit
why: the working kind is the earliest store by source position; the later integer is the conflict (reported at stage 4)

name: q31-earliest-of-two-later-stores
source:
let x = 1
x = "s"
x = true
exit
why: integer first by position; string and boolean are conflicts

name: q31r-written-type-is-the-reference
source:
let x: string = "s"
x = 1
exit
why: a written type is the declaration's reference; the integer store is the conflict

name: q31r-initializer-before-an-earlier-site
source:
let a = 1
let x = "s"
x = a
exit
why: the let's initializer is the declaration whatever the position of the value copied into it later

name: q31r-list-literal-elements-are-the-declaration
source:
let xs = [1, 2]
xs.add("s")
exit
why: for list elements the declaration is the values in the literal; the text store is the error

name: q32a-unknown-after-known-is-held
source:
let x = 1
x = fromJson("1", default: 1)
exit
why: a value the compiler cannot know entering a decided place keeps the runtime check, whatever the order

name: q32a-unknown-before-known-is-held
why: order-free: the same mark when the unknown value comes first

name: q32a-null-default-stays-allowed
source:
let x = null
x = fromJson("1", default: null)
x = 1
exit
why: the owner: `fromJson(..., default: null)` stays allowed beside `let x = null`, `x = 1`; x is integer or null, checked at runtime

name: q32b-known-store-decides
source:
let x = hostValue
x = 1
exit
why: a known store decides a place with an unknown initializer; the host's value keeps the runtime check

name: q32c-null-default-in-a-literal-is-optionality
source:
let ys = [fromJson("t", default: null), 1]
exit
why: Q3.2b in aggregates with the owner's refinement: a known `default: null` contributes optionality to the element

name: q34-read-of-a-certainly-empty-list
source:
let xs = []
let n = xs.first
exit
why: reading the first element of a certainly empty list is a compile error; the read has no value

name: q34-read-of-a-maybe-empty-list-keeps-the-runtime-check
source:
let xs = []
xs.add(1)
let n = xs.first
exit
why: where the list may be empty the read keeps today's runtime check and has the element's type

name: q34-certainly-missing-property
why: a property the object certainly lacks: a compile error, the read has no value

name: q35-late-null-makes-optional
source:
let x = 1
x = null
exit
why: a late null makes the place optional

name: q35-late-null-in-an-element
source:
let xs = [1]
xs.add(null)
exit
why: the same in a part

name: q37-mixed-literal-earliest-kind
source:
let ys = [1, "a"]
let n = ys.first
exit
why: a mixed literal keeps TSV044 and the earliest member's kind is the working kind, so later uses are checked

name: q37-mixed-concatenation
source:
let ys = [1] + ["x"]
exit
why: the orchestrator's scope under Q3.7: a collection built from mixed kinds by `+` takes the earliest operand's kind

name: q38-no-automatic-union
source:
let x = 1
x = fromBase64("YQ==", default: 1)
exit
why: a union that does not fit the working kind is reported at the store; the place stays integer

name: q38-defined-union-first-then-fits
why: the reverse order compiles: the contract's union is the working union and the integer fits it

name: q38-written-union-admits-its-members
source:
let x: integer | string = 1
x = "s"
exit
why: several types in one variable are the author's deliberate act: the written union admits both

name: option-b-conflicting-property-across-literals
source:
let xs = [{a: 1}, {a: "x"}]
exit
why: the owner's option B: property `a` conflicts, the compile error names both values, the earliest kind counts; not a union of two shapes

name: option-b-different-property-sets-are-one-record
source:
let xs = [{x: 1}, {y: "a"}]
let n = xs.first.x
exit
why: different property sets are one record; a read of a property some literal lacks keeps the runtime presence check

name: option-b-reassigned-object-literals
why: two literals of one place are one schema; the conflicting property keeps the earliest kind

name: copy-takes-the-written-type
source:
let a: integer | string = 1
let b = a
b = "s"
exit
why: the owner, 2026-10-18: a copy of a variable with a written type takes that type, so `b = "s"` fits

name: b1-written-union-of-two-collections
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = hostValue
exit
why: each member of a written union keeps its own structure (Dropje97's B1); the host's value is held (Q3.2a)

name: b1-written-union-of-two-lists
source:
let v: integer[] | string[] = hostValue
exit
why: two lists stay two lists, not one list of a union

name: b2-file-order-decides-not-offsets

files.source:
global x = null
x = [1].get(0, default: "s")
exit

why: the second file's store at offset zero does not outrank the first file's defining store (ADR 0021 §1.6, Dropje97's B2a)

name: b2-same-offset-in-two-files-are-two-sites

files.source:
global x = null
x = [1].get(0, default: "s")
exit

why: two `get` expressions at one file-local offset are two defining sites; the boolean is the conflict (Dropje97's B2b), the export the working union

name: q39-method-on-every-member
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = hostValue
let n = v.length
exit
why: a method or property on a union must exist on every member (ADR 3): `length` exists on a list and a set, so the read is valid on both and has one kind

name: q39-method-missing-on-a-member
source:
let v: integer[] | string = hostValue
let n = v.first
exit
why: `first` exists on the list but not on the text: the read is invalid for the text member of the written union (one of the three combinations asked: both members and the host's dynamic view), which the operation's status records for stage 4's report

name: copy-of-a-written-collection-union-keeps-both
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = [1]
let a = v
exit
why: the copy takes the written type, not the initializer's list (PR review r4-B2); no conflict

name: copy-of-a-written-union-accepts-a-member-store
source:
let v: integer[] | string set = [1]
let a = v
a = ["s"].toSet()
exit
why: a later store of the other member fits the copied written type

name: copy-of-a-written-union-excludes-out-of-bound-evidence
source:
let a: integer | string = fromJson("1", default: null)
let b = a
b = "s"
exit
why: the copy takes the written `integer | string` and the held mark (Q3.2a); the initializer's null, outside the bound, is not the copy's evidence

name: b2-two-files-equal-offsets-are-two-bindings
why: two `let x` at offset 0:9 in two files are two bindings; main.tease's is held, other.tease's is not (see the differential's mutation test for the ledger's side)

name: b1-rebuilt-collection-keeps-the-members-apart
why: a collection rebuilt from a written union's member keeps that member's structure (§3.5: a permitted union's members stay their own; Sol's r4-B3): never a list of strings or a set of integers
